statement: A heuristic function h is admissible if for all nodes n, h(n) <= h^*(n), where h(n) is the estimated cost from node n to reach a goal and h^*(n) is the optimal (lowest possible) cost to reach a goal from n.

symbols.meaning: estimated cost from current node n to goal
optimal cost to reach a goal from node n
evaluation function in A* search, defined as f(n) = g(n) + h(n)
cost from the start node to current node n

properties.property: An admissible heuristic acts as a lower bound on the actual cost to reach the goal state.
properties.why: The estimated cost h(n) is always less than or equal to the optimal cost h^*(n) for all nodes n.

properties.property: Guarantees that an informed search algorithm (such as A*) terminates on an optimal path to the goal.
properties.why: The heuristic never overestimates the true remaining cost, preventing suboptimal paths from terminating before optimal paths are explored.

properties.property: All consistent heuristics are admissible, but not all admissible heuristics are consistent.
properties.why: Consistency is a related, stronger condition than admissibility.

properties.property: Guarantee of optimality does not imply search efficiency.
properties.why: An admissible heuristic can guarantee final optimality while not necessarily being efficient.

properties.property: Admissible heuristics can be constructed from problem relaxations, pattern databases of exact subproblem solutions, or inductive learning.
properties.why: Relaxed problems or subproblem pattern databases do not overestimate the cost of the original problem.

assumptions.assumption: The heuristic function is non-negative and never overestimates the lowest possible cost to reach the goal: h(n) <= h^*(n) for all n.
assumptions.breaks_when: The heuristic returns negative values or overestimates the true optimal cost to reach the goal.

assumptions.assumption: The search algorithm progresses candidate paths by lowest evaluation f(n) per iteration and closes all optimal paths before terminating.
assumptions.breaks_when: The search algorithm terminates prematurely without exploring or closing all optimal paths.

failure_modes.mode: Suboptimal path return in A* search
failure_modes.signature: A* terminates on a path with true cost greater than the optimal path cost.
failure_modes.cause: A non-admissible heuristic overestimates remaining cost (h(n) > h^*(n)), causing an overestimation in f(n) that leads the algorithm to overlook the optimal solution.

failure_modes.signature: The algorithm explores an excessively large number of nodes before terminating.
failure_modes.cause: Admissibility guarantees final optimality of the solution path, but does not guarantee computational efficiency.
